2. Notice of 12th Annual General Meeting of the Company 
 
The above documents are being sent through electron ic mode to all the shareholders whose e-mail 
addresses are registered with Depositories/Company/Re gistrar and Share Transfer Agent. The Integrated 
Annual Report and Notice of AGM are also available on the website of the Company at 
www.dalmiabharat.com .

01
Strong
1939
A Bold Vision Before 
Independence 
Long before India achieved its independence, in an era marked by 
uncertainty and limited industrial infrastructure, we planted the 
seeds of a bold vision. In 1939, we established our first cement plant 
in Dalmiapuram, Tamil Nadu - not merely as a business venture, but 
as a commitment to building the nation from the ground up.
We started with a modest capacity of 250 tonnes per day (TPD) 
but what we set in motion was far more significant. We built 
not just a plant, but a foundation of engineering capability, 
resourcefulness and national purpose. Even then, our ambition 
was clear: to be a cornerstone in India’s journey of infrastructure 
and industrialisation.For over eight decades, we have stood as a 
testament to how a deep-rooted commitment to 
nation-building, when combined with a singular 
focus, can evolve into a force of enduring 
strength. From our earliest days, we chose 
to focus on one fundamental pillar ‘cement’ 
because we believed that building India was 
not just about producing material, but about 
laying the foundation for progress, resilience 
and possibility.
1947–1970s 
Building the  
New India
As the country gained independence 
and turned its gaze to infrastructure, 
we scaled with it. Expanding capacities, 
adopting improved processes and 
contributing to landmark public 
projects; our cement helped 
shape the contours of a young and 
ambitious nation.
  Delhi head office in the early 1970's
   Advertisement published in The Times of India 
on August 15, 1947 - India’s Independence Day
We were not just adding tonnes. 
We were building bridges, 
schools, industries and large-scale 
infrastructure projects, quietly 
strengthening India’s backbone.
   Late Shri Jaidayal Dalmia meeting factory 
workers at Dalmiapuram, 1970s.
  Cement bags carried from packaging machines by belt conveyors for truck loading, 1950

1980s–2000s 
Expanding our 
footprint 
As the country gained independence 
and with liberalisation came new 
challenges and opportunities. 
We deepened our capabilities, 
brought in new technologies, and 
began  expanding our geographical 
reach. Cement wasn’t just a 
commodity; it became a symbol of 
scale, consistency and innovation.
By this time, we were operating 
multiple integrated cement plants and 
grinding units across the southern and 
eastern regions of India.2010s
Focused Growth, 
Purposeful 
Direction
We made a conscious decision 
to focus solely on cement. 
Divestments and portfolio 
realignment followed, reinforcing 
our identity as a pure-play cement 
manufacturer. This strategic 
clarity enabled us to channel 
investments, innovation, and 
leadership into one direction scale 
with sustainability.
We crossed 20 
MTPA, then 30, and 
now march towards 
75 MTPA by FY28 
— not as a race 
for volume, but as 
a commitment to 
serve a growing, 
dynamic India.
Today 
Where Scale Meets 
Sustainability
With 15 manufacturing plants, a pan-
India presence, and a strong focus 
on low carbon cement, waste heat 
recovery, and alternative fuels, we 
are not just scaling; we are redefining 
responsible growth.
Our transformation is visible: Tomorrow
Cementing the  
Future with Purpose
As we step into the future, our purpose 
remains unchanged — to build strong 
foundations for generations to come. 
With a target capacity of 110-130 MTPA 
by 2031, and a clear ESG roadmap, we 
are positioned not just as a leading 
cement company, but as a partner in 
India's most iconic projects.

On 12th December 2024, Shuttle 
by Dalmia Bharat, a state-of-the-
art high-performance badminton 
centre at Kalinga Stadium, 
Bhubaneswar, was inaugurated 
by Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, 
Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, 
and Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, 
Hon’ble Chief Minister of Assam 
and President of the Badminton 
Association of India (BAI).
This milestone project reflects a three-way collaboration 
between the Government of Odisha, the Pullela Gopichand 
Badminton Foundation (PGBF), and Dalmia Bharat, aimed at 
building a sustainable and high-impact sporting ecosystem 
in India. Designed and constructed as part of Dalmia Bharat’s 
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives, this facility 
represents a meaningful expansion of our contribution 
to national development; this time through sport and 
youth empowerment.
A purpose-built centre for 
sporting excellence
The facility is home to the Dalmia Bharat Pullela Gopichand 
Badminton Academy, envisioned to become a premier 
training and talent development hub for Indian badminton. 
Architecturally, the centre is inspired by the form of a 
shuttlecock — a first in India for a sports facility — and it 
becomes even more striking at night with specially designed 
rooftop lighting that enhances its presence in the city skyline.
Spread across 77,000 square feet, the indoor complex houses:
• Eight fully air-conditioned badminton courts
• Seating for 400 spectators
• Residential facilities for 36 players within the 
same complex
• A terrace viewing ring offering panoramic views 
of Bhubaneswar
• A walk of fame tracing the history of badminton in India
• An amphitheatre with 200-seat capacity
• A reflective water pool that enhances the visual  
appeal of the structureBuilt with a focus on sustainability
Constructed as part of Dalmia Bharat’s Corporate Social 
Responsibility efforts, the facility has been designed with 
sustainability at its core. It features:
• Rainwater harvesting systems
• Soft paving for groundwater recharge
• Onsite waste recycling initiatives
• An inverted shell design that enhances natural cooling 
and reduces energy consumption
Strength with purpose
The inauguration of Shuttle by Dalmia Bharat marks more 
than the creation of a high-performance centre; it is a 
continuation of our legacy of contributing to the nation’s 
progress. From building bridges and stadiums to nurturing 
champions of tomorrow, our journey is defined by a singular 
goal: strengthening India’s future.
As we move forward, we  
remain committed to doing what 
we have always done, building 
with purpose and standing  
strong with India.
Contributing to India’s  
infrastructure progress in FY25
‘Shuttle by  
Dalmia Bharat’
An architecture marvel and a vision for 
Indian badminton excellence

SecureA governance 
philosophy 
grounded in 
trust
Our approach to governance is built on 
the belief that transparency and ethical 
decision-making are essential drivers 
of sustained stakeholder confidence. 
Governance is not just a function 
but a shared responsibility across all 
levels of the organisation. The Board 
of Directors plays an active role in 
shaping the Company’s long-term 
strategy, ensuring strong oversight 
in areas like ESG commitments and 
risk management.
A culture anchored in 
ethics and accountability
A secure organisation is built on 
ethical practices. Our Code of Conduct 
serves as a living document that 
sets clear behavioural expectations, 
defines accountability, and promotes 
responsible conduct across the 
organisation. Ethics are not just 
enforced; they are internalised 
through dialogue, training and 
regular reinforcement.Training for governance 
at every level
Good governance evolves with the 
capabilities of those who practice it. 
We conduct multiple training initiatives 
to strengthen awareness around 
regulatory changes, ESG integration 
and data protection practices. 
These included:
• Code of Conduct refreshers across 
all employee levels
• Targeted risk and compliance 
training for key functions
• Governance updates and ESG 
orientation for the Board and 
senior management
By embedding governance at every 
level, we ensure it becomes integral 
to decision-making and upholding 
our values.
Prepared for the future
In FY25, our commitment to secure 
operations was driven not just by 
compliance, but by character. As we 
look ahead, we remain focused on 
strengthening governance frameworks, 
enhancing data governance and 
cybersecurity preparedness, and 
continuously upskilling our teams 
to respond to emerging risks. 
Our practices are evolving in alignment 
with global standards while staying true 
to the values that have long guided us.
  Training session in progress at Guwahati Cement Works Jagiroad (Assam)In a rapidly changing world, being secure 
at Dalmia Bharat goes beyond protecting 
assets; it is about building trust, ensuring 
good governance, and strengthening lasting 
relationships. In FY25, amidst shifting industry 
dynamics and rising stakeholder expectations, 
we remained secure and stable, thanks 
to disciplined governance, long-term risk 
preparedness, a culture of care, accountability 
and ethics.

03
Sustainable
Circularity 
across the 
value  chain 
Circular economy has become a central 
pillar of our sustainability strategy, 
focusing on resource efficiency, 
waste reduction, and material 
reuse. This year, we have prioritised 
embedding circularity across all 
operations. In cement manufacturing, 
we are reducing reliance on virgin 
materials and lowering carbon 
emissions by innovatively using fly ash, 
slag, and blended cements, directly 
supporting our decarbonisation goals.
6.4  MnT
Fly ash used
4.5  MnT
Slag used
Driving decarbonisation 
through circular solutions
While circular economy forms the 
core of our efforts, decarbonisation 
continues to be a key focus. We are 
advancing carbon capture technologies 
and exploring alternative fuels to lower 
emissions further. These efforts are 
seamlessly integrated into our circular 
economy strategy, where reducing 
carbon impact and reusing materials 
go hand in hand.
Read More  Pg 86
Managing waste 
and enhancing 
resource efficiency
Waste management is another key 
area of focus. In FY25, we deepened 
our commitment to systematic waste 
management by improving our waste 
tracking systems and expanding 
our recycling efforts. We also made 
progress towards reducing plastic 
use by transitioning to recycled 
polypropylene bags for packaging. 
This initiative is an important step 
in our ongoing journey towards 
supporting a circular economy.
Circularity in mining 
and packaging
Our dedication to circularity extends 
beyond cement production. In mining, 
we have repurposed sub-threshold 
waste rock for civil construction, 
making better use of materials and 
reducing the environmental footprint. 
In packaging, our use of recycled 
polypropylene bags is a step toward 
closing the loop on plastic waste.
Global collaborations and 
driving collective impact
We continue to work closely with 
global sustainability leaders, including 
our active participation in the G20 
Resource Efficiency and Circular 
Economy Industry Coalition (RECEIC). 
These partnerships help us stay at the 
forefront of circular economy trends, 
share best practices, and accelerate 
collective action toward a more 
sustainable future.Over the years, we have focused on multiple 
dimensions of sustainability, including reducing 
carbon emissions, optimising resource use, and 
advancing community development. While we 
continued to strengthen our decarbonisation 
initiatives and focus on waste reduction, 
this year we further reinforced our focus on 
circular economy as a transformative approach 
to sustainability.

Our management remains accountable for the accuracy 
and reliability of the information disclosed in this Report. 
It assures that the Report comprehensively covers all material 
topics impacting the organisation and its stakeholders, 
demonstrating the organisation's approach to leveraging 
opportunities while managing risks. The methodology for 
calculating certain Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) has been 
revised. As a result, figures presented for previous years may 
differ from those disclosed in earlier reports.

on May 30, 2025.Materiality

operations
We have one of the lowest

industry, at just 456 kgCO₂ per

further demonstrated through our 
RE100, EP100 and EV100 initiatives

First in the cement industry to

assessment from SEBI licensed ERP.Innovative  
product portfolio

reflects our commitment to specialised

integrity and durability. As part of 
this focus, the share of our premium 
products increased from 21% in FY24 
to 23% in FY25, demonstrating our 
emphasis on higher-margin and value-
added products.
As one of India’s largest producers of 
Portland Slag Cement (PSC), we utilise 
slag to create sustainable blended 
cements. With a goal of increasing our 
blended cement production, our focus 
on premiumisation and innovation 
positions us as a preferred choice for 
high quality construction.

Dalmia Bharat Limited
In a fast-changing business environment, we have built our 
growth story on the foundation of operational strength, 
robust governance and a strong commitment to sustainability. 
These principles guide our decisions, inspire our actions and 
define the legacy we are creating for the future.
Our Honourable Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi once 
said, “We will naturally pursue our goals but we know that 
we will be more successful when we do this in partnership 
with the world.” Despite the recent global uncertainties, 
the economic prospects and partnerships of India have 
brightened as the country is expected to be a major 
beneficiary of higher FDI inflows, creation of large-scale 
manufacturing infrastructure and thus ensuing greater 
employment generation. The recently-concluded trade 
agreements with the United Kingdom, along with ongoing 
negotiations with the United States, are expected to further 
contribute to the country's economic growth.
India remains one of the fastest-growing economies in the 
world with a projected GDP growth rate of 6.5% in 2025-26. 
The country is adding incremental trillion dollar to its economy 
faster than ever and this economic momentum is expected 
to support cement demand in the years ahead. Despite being 
the world’s second-largest cement producer, India's average 
per capita cement consumption remains around 295 kg, well 
below the global average of 500 kg, indicating significant 
headroom for growth.
FY25 witnessed a subdued cement demand growth of around 
5% YoY amidst the general elections in the country, key state 
elections and erratic rains during the year. We believe that 
the demand growth will bounce back to 7-8% YoY in FY26 
driven by healthy demand from all key drivers-housing, 
infrastructure building and private investments. The year is 
also expected to benefit with stronger pricing and a focus on 
cost savings.
Sectoral consolidation to continue
With regards to the overall installed cement capacity, over the 
last two decades, the industry has grown at a CAGR of 5-6%. 
Within this, during the last three years, the pace of sector 
consolidation has increased and the capacity share of the top 
four companies has grown considerably from approximately 
48% in 2021-22 to nearly 58% in 2024-25. In FY25, alone, we 
witnessed 52 million tonnes of capacity changing hands.During the next couple of years, the supply is expected to 
grow at 7-8% CAGR, which could possibly keep the sector 
capacity utilisation at its current levels. Within this, the 
industry leaders will continue to expand at a faster pace, 
and are thus expected to enhance their capacity share to 
more than 60% in the next two years.
STRONG
The foundation of our growth
“In uncertain times, the strongest  
foundations are not those made of concrete, 
but of conviction.”
Our growth journey is underpinned by a clear vision-to build 
scale, efficiency and market leadership. We continue to invest 
in expanding our production capabilities, diversifying our 
geographical footprint and adopting innovative solutions that 
enhance productivity and cost competitiveness.
During the year, we have added 4.9 MTPA of cement capacity 
across our operating locations and with this we have achieved 
the Phase 1 of our expansion milestone of 49.5 MTPA. 
Our Phase II expansion strategy will further reinforce our 
position as a pan-India pure-play cement player, placing 
us favourably on track to achieve our long term target of 
110-130 MTPA. The journey ahead will be a mix of organic 
and inorganic capacity addition with more focus on planned 
and systematic organic growth.
As part of Phase II expansion, we have announced plans to 
invest  I 3,520 crore over the next two years and add 3 MTPA 
cement capacity each in Pune and Belgaum. While the Pune 
unit will cater to the untapped Western Maharashtra markets, 
the Belgaum Unit will improve penetration into the Southern 
Maharashtra markets.
During FY25, while our cement volumes grew by 2% on 
YoY basis, the overall revenue declined by 4.8% YoY to 
I 13,980 crore and EBITDA stood at I 2,407 crore. The volume 
growth was lower than the likely industry growth since 
we discontinued the tolling volumes from the plants of 
Jaiprakash Associates Limited from June 2024. We also 
witnessed considerable price weakness through the year in 
FY25, across our key operating regions, a trend which we now 
see reversing.

Dalmia Bharat is proud to be amongst the lowest total cost

and optimising and digitalising our supply chain. In the 
ongoing fiscal, we will see much of these efficiency gains 
flowing in.

expanding the use of automation and smart technology 
across our entire value chain. Solutions like Automated 
Vendor Invoice Management, Transport Management and 
the digitisation of various HR functions are minimising human 
intervention, enhancing control and driving efficiency.
SECURE
Stability, governance and trust
Trust is not built over night, it is the outcome of consistent 
delivery, ethical practices and responsible governance. 
At Dalmia Bharat, our emphasis on security goes beyond 
financial stability. It encompasses the systems we build, 
the transparency we uphold and the trust we nurture with 
employees, partners and communities.
To ensure optimal utilisation of our capital resources 
while maintaining the strength of our balance sheet, we 
have divested the majority of our non-core assets in a 
phased manner and now operate within the well-defined guardrails laid down under the Capital Allocation Framework. 
This disciplined approach has enabled us to consistently 
scale capacity year after year, while keeping leverage well 
below industry norms. In FY25, we added 4.9 MnT of cement 
capacity through a combination of greenfield and brownfield 
expansions, while maintaining a Net Debt/EBITDA ratio 
of 0.3x.
People are the cornerstone of any business and hence 
building a younger team with a caring culture and enabling 
our employees to excel in their life and career remains a key 
priority for me. With a strong focus on growth of our people, 
we launched several structured development initiatives 
this year, tailored to different career stages, from frontline 
employees to senior leaders. Notable programmes include 
DRIVE and DRON. We are also executing a robust succession 
planning process for critical roles, ensuring smooth transitions 
from retiring leaders to young talent. In parallel, we are 
actively inducting management trainees across functions and 
locations to strengthen our entry-level pipeline.
As one of the real vanguards of the cement business in India, 
Dalmia Bharat is constantly trying to adopt modern practices 
to continuously strengthen our workplace safety, and foster 
a safer and quality working environment. We are undertaking 
a safety excellence programme across our operations to 
enhance the effectiveness of our safety SOPs, avoid unsafe 
practices and embed a stronger safety culture. 
Our vision to build a transparent, industry-leading 
organisation over the next decade rests on an aligned 
leadership team and a deeply motivated workforce. During 
the year, we strengthened our operational risk controls and 
internal compliance systems to foster greater agility and 
transparency across the organisation.
SUSTAINABLE
A commitment to the future
We believe that true progress must also be regenerative. 
Our long-standing commitment to sustainability is deeply 
woven into our business model - from producing low-carbon 
cement to advancing circularity and renewable energy 
integration. We view environmental stewardship 
as a compliance and a responsibility.Operating in a ‘hard-to-abate’ sector, we have been at the 
forefront of the cement industry’s transition to a low-carbon 
future. We continuously invest in decarbonising our value 
chain and have one of the lowest net carbon footprints 
across the global cement industry at 456 kg CO2 per ton of 
cementitious material. We are also first cement group aspiring 
to be carbon Negative by 2040.
We made significant strides towards minimising the use 
of natural resources. Today, our total cement production 
consists 84% of blended cement – which is produced using 
alternative raw materials like slag and fly ash. We are also 
gradually switching from traditional electricity sources like 
coal-based power plants to renewable energy. During FY25, 
we have increased our Renewable power capacity by 82 MW 
to 267 MW and remain on track to achieve 595 MW by the 
end of FY26.
As part of our RE100 commitment, we have already 
achieved a fourfold increase in renewable energy 
consumption compared to the RE100 baseline and are 
committed to a 100% renewable energy transition in the 
long term.
Our sustainability initiatives go much beyond environmental 
stewardship to encompass social responsibility. Our  focused 
interventions across the chosen areas of education, 
healthcare, skill development and community empowerment 
enrich the lives of more than 1.25 lakh individuals every 
year across 11 states. Our initiative – Gram Parivartan, has 
now scaled to 30+ community development programmes, 
promoting inclusive growth through livelihoods, health 
and education. We aspire to continue making a meaningful 
difference wherever we operate by creating sustainable, 
inclusive and resilient communities.
We are pleased to share that we have appointed ICRA, 
a SEBI Category-I ESG Rating Provider, for our ESG rating. 
The Company has been assigned a Combined ESG Rating 
of 78 (Strong), derived from an Impact Rating of 71 (Good) 
and a Transition Rating of 84 (Accelerating). In addition our 
score in S&P Global CSA Score has further improved to 64, 
demonstrating our commitment towards sustainability.CONCLUSION
As a nation, we are fortunate to witness and be part of this 
period of rapid growth, with the cement sector playing a 
key role in the Viksit Bharat vision. In the next fiscal, our 
key priorities will include accelerating capacity expansion 
to strengthen our position as a pan-India player, optimising 
existing assets, building strong brand equity, and deepening 
our cost leadership.
As we move ahead, we convey our heartfelt gratitude to all 
our people and our stakeholders for their continuous support 
and immense faith in us. Together, we are building a company 
that is strong in execution, secure in its values and sustainable 
in its impact
Thank you. Jai Hind.

Governance 
Management approach to ESG
At Dalmia Bharat, sustainability is not just a priority - it is 
integral to how we operate and grow. Our business strategy 
is designed to create long-term value while upholding our 
environmental, social, and governance (ESG) responsibilities. 
We believe responsible business practices, sound governance, 
and proactive ESG leadership are essential to building trust 
and delivering long-term benefits for all our stakeholders - 
customers, employees, communities, suppliers, shareholders, 
and the government.
The short, mid and long-term strategy on ESG, is presented 
to the board by the key management from various domains 
and the Board reviews and approves the strategy along 
with financial and capital budgets, with progress tracked on 
quarterly basis. The Risk Management Committee oversees 
ESG-related risks, while the CSR Committee leads our social 
impact agenda. The Chief Risk Officer ensures effective risk 
policy implementation, and our sustainability department 
drives strategy, materiality, stakeholder ESG engagements, 
and on-ground initiatives.
Cyber security resilience
At Dalmia Bharat, safeguarding information assets and 
ensuring cyber resilience is at the core of our operations. 
In response to the dynamic cyber threat landscape, we have 
adopted a comprehensive cyber security strategy covering 
IT, OT, cloud and data security. We continuously strengthen 
our controls, raise user awareness and benchmark against 
industry best practices to stay ahead of evolving threats.

External Environment 
Responding to changing  
industry dynamics
In FY25, we proactively responded to shifting market dynamics. India’s 
infrastructure expansion, rising housing demand and sustainability 
imperatives continue to shape our operating landscape. We focused on 
operational excellence, innovation and resource optimisation to navigate 
industry challenges and seize emerging opportunities. 
Growing cement demand   
India's cement demand is projected to experience robust growth, 
with forecasts indicating an increase from 424 MnT in FY24 to 
over 640 MnT by FY30. This growth, representing a compound 
annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 7-8%, is primarily 
driven by rising infrastructure development and construction 
activities across the country.  
Real estate sector dynamics  
The real estate sector continues to be a significant driver 
of cement consumption. The government aims to build 
20 million affordable homes over the next five years. 
This initiative is expected to substantially boost cement 
demand in the residential segment.

Risk Management
Building resilience  in a 
changing environment
As an organisation, we are committed to safeguard our business 
against evolving challenges while enabling sustainable growth. 
Our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework is designed 
to proactively identify, assess, and mitigate risks across strategic, 
operational, financial, compliance and sustainability domains.
Enterprise Risk Management  
Our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) function enables 
the achievement of our Company’s strategic objectives by 
identifying, analysing, assessing, mitigating, monitoring and 
governing any risks or potential threats to these objectives. 
The foundation of our ERM activities lies in our values, culture 
and commitment. Our ERM system is built on a resilience 
perspective, supporting both the survival and sustainable 
growth of the business.
For our existing operations and ongoing projects, risks are 
identified at the Company level and further detailed at 
the plant level using a consistently applied methodology. 
We have constituted a Risk Council at the plant level to 
enhance understanding of the risk framework. The plant and 
operations teams are actively involved in identifying risks 
relevant to their specific operations, and risk registers are 
maintained for each plant. These efforts are supported by 
regular review meetings to track mitigation progress and 
identify any new or emerging risks.
Risk governance structure 
“Our risk management approach is 
integrated into our strategic planning 
and decision-making processes. Through 
regular assessments, we ensure that 
risks are managed proactively, aligning 
with our commitment to long-term value 
creation and stakeholder trust.”
Rajiv Choubey
Group General Counsel 
and Chief Risk Officer
Scope, context and criteria for 
risk process
Defining the scope of the process after 
understanding the internal and external 
context within Dalmia Bharat’s risk appetite
Risk identification
Identification of sources of risk, areas of 
impact, events and their causes along 
with their potential consequences on the 
achievement of business objectives
Risk analysis, evaluation 
and prioritisation
Evaluate and assess the potential impact, 
likelihood and velocity of the identified risks 
and prioritise risks based on the risk rating to 
identify key risks
Risk treatment
It involves the process of planning and 
implementing risk mitigation plans response 
strategies and assessing the effectiveness of 
the treatment
Risk monitoring and reporting
The status of the risks needs to be monitored 
periodically, given the changing external 
environment, and the key enterprise risks 
must be reported on a periodic basis to 
evaluate the progress of mitigation plansRisk management framework 
and process
We have implemented an enterprise-wide risk management 
programme and framework in line with international standards 
such as COSO ERM 2017 and ISO 31000:2018. A combination 
of top-down and bottom-up approaches are used to identify, 
assess, monitor and mitigate risks by risk champions and owners 
across the Group. The Risk Management Committee (RMC), a 
sub-committee of the Board, oversees the programme, and a 
Chief Risk Officer has been appointed to drive ERM initiatives. Risk management Committee
The Risk Management Committee (the Committee) is 
formed by Independent Directors of the Company. As on 
March 31, 2024, the Committee comprised:
Mr Paul Heinz Hugentobler

Objectives and responsibilities of the Risk Management 
Committee are:
• To Identify and document new and emerging risks for 
the unit/function, and contributing factors to the risks 
identified, through focused discussions with stakeholders 
within the unit/function.
• Document and update the existing controls implemented 
within the unit/function to mitigate the identified risk.
• Escalation of challenges, concerns or unforeseen 
developments pertaining to existing or emerging risk(s) to 
the Manufacturing head and informing/updating to CRO.
• To assist the Board in fulfilling its corporate governance 
oversight responsibilities with regard to the identification, 
evaluation and mitigation of strategic, operational and 
external environment risks.
• To monitor and approve the enterprise risk management 
framework and associated practices of the Company.
• To evaluate significant risk exposures of the Company and 
assess the actions to mitigate exposures.
• To review and reassess the adequacy of the Risk 
Management Committee Charter periodically and 
recommend any proposed changes to the Board 
for approval.

Materiality Assessment
Keeping sustainability  
at the core
We undertook a comprehensive double materiality assessment in 
FY25 to strategically meet our sustainability goals. It has enabled 
us to enhance organisational resilience, allocate resources 
judiciously and safeguard stakeholder interests.  
Materiality assessment, 
approach and methodology
The double materiality assessment follows a rigorous and 
structured process, integrating both financial and impact 
materiality. This approach recognises how sustainability 
issues impact the Company (outside-in), as well as how the 
Company's operations and strategies affect the environment 
and society (inside-out). The assessment was captured in 
stakeholder feedback gathered from a diverse group of 
internal and external stakeholders, including employees, 
suppliers, customers and industry associations.
A total of 21 material topics were initially identified through a 
combination of sector-specific knowledge and benchmarking, 
global standards and frameworks and secondary research. 
These topics covered key Environmental, Social, and 
Governance (ESG) themes that are relevant to our business 
and the broader cement and construction industry.Materiality matrix
Prioritising and ranking material topics
All 21 topics were shared with stakeholders for ranking based 
on their perceived importance and relevance. Each topic was 
scored on two key dimensions: Severity , which represents 
the extent of potential impact and Likelihood , indicating the 
probability of occurrence. The scores were then processed 
through a structured methodology, where a Risk Priority 
Number (RPN) was calculated for each topic. To enhance 
comparability and clarity, a descaling process was applied to 
normalise scores across all inputs.
Outcome of materiality assessment
The adjusted RPN values helped to prioritise material 
topics. This helped to identify material issues which will 
directly impact our sustainability strategy, risk management 
framework and disclosures. The double materiality 
assessment ensures alignment with global best practices 
and regulatory expectations while also remaining attuned 
to the concerns and expectations of stakeholders. It serves 
as a strategic tool for driving informed decision-making and 
enhancing long-term resilience and value creation.

Resilient performance
The year began on a relatively slow note, with the general 
elections in the first quarter and heavy monsoons in the 
second quarter moderating economic activity and output. 
However, from the third quarter onwards, we witnessed 
a steady revival in demand, supported by a pickup in 
construction activities, improved rural sentiment, increased 
momentum in the real estate sector and higher government 
expenditure. This recovery enabled us to grow our volumes 
by 2% on a year-on-year basis.
At the same time, the industry environment remained 
competitive, with pricing pressure emerging. These dynamics 
had a bearing on our revenue performance during the year.We were able to withstand intense 
pricing pressures in FY25 through 
sustainable improvements in our 
controllable operating metrics. 
Our disciplined approach to capital 
allocation also ensured a strong 
balance sheet by keeping net debt 
in check. These actions have laid 
a solid foundation for the next 
phase of growth and long-term 
value creation.

FY23Capital structure and  
debt management
As of March 31, 2025, our gross debt stood at ₹5,279 crore, 
with net debt at ₹716 crore, resulting in a net debt-to-EBITDA 
ratio of 0.30. The increase in leverage was driven by strategic 
investments for capacity expansion. Despite a temporary rise 
in debt, we have ensured financial prudence, with a focus on 
maintaining a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio below 2.0x, to sustain 
a balanced capital structure.
Cash flow and liquidity management
Our proactive approach to cash flow management, including 
improved receivables collection and vendor invoice factoring, 
ensures robust liquidity. This enables us to fund strategic 
investments and maintain a healthy balance sheet.
Strategic debt management
In FY25, we raised long-term rupee term loans to support 
capacity expansion, resulting in a modest increase in our 
debt-equity ratio. Despite this, our financial leverage remains 
within a comfortable range, ensuring sustained growth for 
the Company.

FY23Shareholder returns 
We are committed to providing sustainable returns to our 
shareholders. As part of our disciplined capital allocation 
framework, we allocate up to 10% of our operating cash flow 
to shareholder returns, including dividends and share buybacks. 
In FY25, we declared an interim dividend of ₹4 per share and 
recommended a final dividend of ₹5 per share, reinforcing our 
commitment to delivering value while maintaining financial 
flexibility for growth.
Focused capital allocation 
We are actively investing in greenfield and brownfield 
expansion projects to scale our cement production capacity 
in line with long-term market demand. These investments are 
directed towards setting up integrated plants, clinker units 
and grinding facilities in strategically important locations. 
Each project is chosen with a focus on long-term cost 
competitiveness and logistical advantages.
Operational and cost excellence
Alongside growth, we are deploying capital to improve 
operating efficiency and reduce production costs. Key 
initiatives include debottlenecking of existing plants, 
modernisation of equipment, and selective upgrades to 
improve throughput and reliability.
Innovation and green energy fund
We have committed up to 10% of our operating cash flow 
towards an Innovation and Green Energy Fund. This fund is 
dedicated to advancing focused research and development in 
climate change solutions and emerging technologies. Through 
this initiative, we aim to accelerate our transition to cleaner 
energy, drive long term sustainability and strengthen our 
leadership in low carbon manufacturing.
Disciplined capital allocation framework
All capex decisions follow a structured evaluation process 
to ensure optimal return on investment and alignment with 
our long-term financial goals. Our capex is funded through a 
prudent mix of internal accruals and debt, with a continued 
focus on maintaining a robust balance sheet and strong 
credit metrics.
Managing financial risks
We proactively manage key financial risks through a 
structured Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) approach. 
To mitigate notable financial risks such as macro-economic 
factors (inflation, supply chain disruptions, interest rates), 
regulatory changes and commodity price fluctuations 
(such as coal and pet coke), we have strengthened supply 
chain resilience, optimised our fuel mix and focused on 
local sourcing to manage risks effectively.  Belgaum Plant, Karnataka

Ganesh W Jirkuntwar
National Manufacturing HeadCapacity expansion
To cater to growing demand and enhance operational 
leverage, we scaled up both cement and clinker capacities.
Cement capacity expansion
We enhanced our cement production capacity by 4.9 MTPA in 
FY25 across four units.
Lanka:  A new 2.4 MTPA cement grinding unit was 
commissioned, expanding scale to our southern footprint.
Ariyalur:  Capacity was enhanced by 1 MTPA through 
infrastructure upgrades and improved material 
handling systems.
Kadapa:  An additional 1 MTPA cement capacity was 
added, aligned with clinker availability and grinding 
process optimisation.
Rohtas:  We commissioned 0.5 MTPA additional capacity to 
strengthen market responsiveness in the eastern region.
Clinker capacity enhancement
We expanded clinker capacity by 0.9 MTPA in FY25 through 
debottlenecking projects at Rajgangpur and Kadapa.
Rajgangpur:  Clinker capacity increased by 0.6 MTPA by installing 
a 250 tonne per hour, hydraulic roller press (TPH HRP) which 
increased output to 10,500 tonne per day (TPD). Additionally, 
the cyclone chamber was replaced by a high-efficiency twin 
cyclone which reduced return dust from 14.8% to 8%.
Kadapa:  Clinker capacity expanded by 0.3 MTPA, resulting in 
kiln output from 6,100 to 7,000 TPD and enabling us to support 
35% refuse derived fuel (RDF) usage. We also installed a larger 
top cyclone, upgraded preheater fan and a new Pyrojet burner 
to increase efficiency.  Celebrating excellence in manufacturing, Line 3, Rajgangpur (Odisha)At Dalmia Bharat, we focus on 
strengthening our manufacturing

technologies and optimising resource 
use to drive operational resilience and 
agility. Our efforts have boosted capacity 
expansion and empowered us to align 
growth objectives with our commitment to 
responsible production.

Dalmia Cement PQM Laboratory and

Dalmia Cement’s Product Quality Monitoring (PQM)

Ensuring fuel efficiency
Fuel efficiency was a key focus area, with a particular 
emphasis on reducing fossil fuel usage and better thermal 
integration. We implemented several technical upgrades 
and process improvements to reduce fuel costs and enhance 
kiln performance:
• Increased recycled waste absorption in kilns, replacing 
fossil fuels with alternative fuels like MSW and 
hazardous waste.
• High-efficiency clinker cooler installed at Kadapa improved 
heat recuperation and reduced thermal load.
• Twin cyclone system replaced existing CCX at Rajgangpur 
Line III, leading to a 7-8 kcal/kg clinker saving.
• Cooler operations were optimised at Belgaum to reduce 
clinker loss, contributing to substantial clinker savings.
• Blending strategies were fine-tuned to maximise use of 
green fuels, lowering average fuel costs.
Pre-processing  
systems
Improvement of WHRS 
We strategically utilised kiln shutdown periods to upgrade 
equipment and upgrade the WHRS (Waste Heat Recovery 
System). This allowed us to improve energy recovery without 
disrupting production output.
• WHRS performance was enhanced by optimising boiler 
inlet temperatures, bypass dampers, and cement 
process parameters.
• These efforts led to an increase of 5 crore units in WHRS 
power generation, now contributing to 2% of our total 
energy needs.Sustainable manufacturing 
Product portfolio optimisation
In response to market expectations and sustainability 
imperatives, we commenced production of Portland 
Composite Cement (PCC) at four key plants: Dalmiapuram, 
Ariyalur, Kadapa and Lanka. This shift is aligned with our 
efforts to lower the clinker factor and reduce carbon 
intensity while catering to growing demand for green 
construction materials.

manufacturing 
Operational reliability with 
Industry  4.0 technologies
As part of our digital transformation journey, all 15 
Dalmia Cement plants have been equipped with advanced 
Predictive Maintenance Systems, integrated with Industry 
4.0 technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet 
of Things (IoT) and remote automation. This transition 
represents a major leap toward data-driven efficiency, 
proactive equipment management and enhanced 
plant reliability.
Approximately 2,692 AI-based auto-diagnostic sensors have 
been strategically installed to monitor equipment health, 
ensure early fault detection and initiate preventive measures, 
much ahead of actual breakdowns.
Key enablers of predictive maintenance
The successful deployment of this system is backed by a 
strong ecosystem of centralised and intelligent capabilities: 
• DCBL reliability team:  Centrally governs the monitoring 
framework and oversees real-time performance 
across plants.• IU support:  Facilitates advanced fault analytics and real-
time equipment health monitoring for early intervention.
• Centralised data access:  A unified digital platform 
consolidates operational data from all sites, enabling quick 
and informed decision-making.
• Remote diagnostics:  Enables expert-led, off-site 
troubleshooting, reducing the time and effort required for 
on-ground intervention.
• Asset digitisation:  Comprehensive digital mapping of 
critical assets supports lifecycle tracking, predictive 
maintenance and inventory optimisation.
Benefits
The predictive maintenance ecosystem has resulted 
in measurable benefits across operational and 
safety parameters:
• Real-time health scoring of assets supports timely 
corrective actions
• Unplanned equipment breakdowns and surprise stoppages 
have been significantly reduced
• Improved spare parts planning and optimised 
inventory management
• Enhanced worker safety through early fault detection

Intellectual Capital
Pioneering industrial carbon capture 
in India
In alignment with India’s net zero commitment and the Paris 
Agreement, the Department of Science and Technology (DST), 
Government of India, launched a focused call to accelerate 
Carbon Capture and Utilisation technologies within the 
cement sector.
We are proud to have been selected—alongside the Indian 
Institute of Technology Bombay—as an award recipient 
under this programme. Together, we are designing and 
commissioning an industrial test bed at our Rajgangpur 
facility, supported by DST. This pilot will capture CO₂ directly 
from the kiln stack using our proprietary water-based 
catalyst, and convert it into stable carbonates through 
mineralisation reactors.
The installation is designed to capture over 2,000 kg of CO₂ 
per day—meeting the DST threshold for industrial validation. 
Over a three-year cycle, the project will be optimised 
for reaction conditions, energy efficiency, and market 
applicability of mineralised outputs. By proving feasibility at 
this scale, we aim to de-risk technology commercialisation 
and enable broader deployment across the cement industry.
Upcycling waste into high-
performance materials
Our R&D team has created a thermochemical method 
that transforms low-grade limestone, previously deemed 
non-utilisable, into a high-performance Supplementary 
Cementitious Material (SCM). Independent tests using X-ray 
diffraction and differential scanning calorimetry confirmed 
that the amorphous phase surpasses 99%.
We are currently evaluating:
• The material’s performance under accelerated 
carbonation curing
• Synergies with other SCMs such as fly ash and 
calcined clays
• Scale-up feasibility, focusing on energy integration and 
morphological consistencyAligning digital strategy with

  Quality lab at Rohtas Cement Works (Bihar)Driving maintenance innovation to 
boost shredder output
Unit: Ariyalur
Department:  Recycle waste
Team:  Mr. Jeyabalan, Mr. Sathishkumar, Mr. Saravanan, 
Mr. Induvasan, Mr. George Benny
As part of our Dalmia Dil Se programme, a frontline 
team from the Ariyalur unit demonstrated how ground-
level innovation can lead to measurable impact. Facing 
persistent performance challenges in waste shredding 
operations, the team reimagined their maintenance 
practices to unlock better efficiency.
Challenge and context
The unit’s high-capacity shredders process Refuse-Derived 
Fuel (RDF) and Multi-Layered Plastics (MLP), often mixed 
with moisture, sand, and stones. This caused rapid and 
excessive wear of blades, frequent breakdowns, and 
reduced output. In-situ repairs were time-consuming and 
often ineffective, hampering throughput and increasing 
clinker variable costs.Solution
The team implemented a new maintenance strategy, 
including:
• Shifting from in-situ repair to external refurbishment 
of rotors and combs.
• Introducing a rotation model using spare assemblies 
to reduce downtime.
• Improving blade fabrication with water jet cutting 
and plug welding.
• Applying tungsten carbide coatings to enhance 
blade durability.
Impact
Output: Improved from 10 TPH to 18–20 TPH.
Downtime: Reduced from 216 hours to 96 hours over 
a 45-day cycle.
Efficiency: Achieved higher TSR% and better 
cost optimisation.
Recognition: Appreciated by the CTO team and shared 
across other units for wider implementation.CASE STUDY

Environmental management system
The Environmental Management System (EMS), based on 
the ISO 14001 framework and the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle 
(PDCA), plays a central role in implementing our ESG Policy. 
Responsibility for EMS execution lies directly with the facility 
head, supported by an appointed management representative 
at each site. Department-specific Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs) are in place to guide environmental 
practices in line with operational exposure and requirements. 
The EMS is designed to drive continuous improvement, 
with a strong focus on setting measurable targets to 
reduce our environmental footprint and enhance overall 
sustainability performance.Monitoring environmental performance
We have established a system to track capital investments, 
expenses, cost savings and cost avoidance linked to our 
environmental initiatives. This allows for effective monitoring 
of financial impacts at both facility and Group levels, with 
100% coverage across our operations. 
Climate strategy
Our climate strategy adopts a comprehensive framework 
for deep decarbonisation, integrating circular economy 
principles, renewable energy and emerging low-carbon 
technologies. These include Carbon Capture and 
Utilisation (CCU), sustainable biomass, mineralisation and 
heat electrification. We are committed to science-based 
targets, working to lower our carbon footprint through 
enhanced energy efficiency, low-carbon cement adoption 
and increased use of recycled waste.

GHG emissions
Reducing GHG emissions is a core priority for us, and we have 
introduced various measures to address it, fully recognising its 
importance to our operations.Emission monitoring and 
control technologies
We have developed a robust emissions management system 
to monitor and reduce emissions throughout our operations. 
Our Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) deliver 
real-time data on emissions, helping us ensure regulatory 
compliance and enabling us to take swift corrective actions 
when necessary. To further enhance our environmental 
oversight, we have also installed a Continuous Ambient Air 
Quality Monitoring Station (CAAQMS) to continuously track 
air quality and reinforce our commitment to sustainable 
environmental practices.
Moderation of air emissions
We have introduced several innovative technologies aimed 
at minimising our environmental impact, including the 
optimisation of burning zone temperatures, the use of 
low-NOx calciners and burners, and the deployment of 
electrostatic precipitators and baghouses for efficient dust 
control. Preventive measures, such as covering conveyor belts 
and storage areas and using mechanised sweeping machines, 
have also been implemented to reduce fugitive dust 
emissions. In addition, we are progressively incorporating 
electric vehicles into our fleet to reduce air emissions from 
transport and raw material handling.15.33  Mn tCO2e

Renewable energy
As part of our commitment to expanding the use of

capacity. In addition, we have begun purchasing hydropower 
and sourcing renewable electricity to further support our

Renewable energy acquisition
In line with our commitment to deep decarbonisation 
and energy transition, we have strategically leveraged 
group captive renewable energy projects to power our 
cement operations with clean energy. As of FY2025, we 
have commissioned 59 MW of renewable energy capacity-
comprising wind and solar-under the group captive 
model. This is in addition to 136 MW own solar capacity 
and 72 MW waste recovery based capacity. The initiative 
supports our broader goal of sourcing 100% renewable 
electricity, while also enhancing energy security and cost 
stability. The group captive route enables co-ownership of 
renewable assets, offering both financial and environmental 
benefits by offsetting Scope 1&2 emissions and reducing 
dependency on fossil based electricity. These projects 
have significantly contributed to increasing our renewable 
electricity share, which now stands at 36% of our total 
power consumption, and play a vital role in our pathway 
toward becoming a carbon-negative company by 2040. 
Dalmia Cement's group captive strategy also exemplifies 
how  industry can collaboratively accelerate India’s renewable 
energy targets while embedding climate leadership in core

Circular economy
We have implemented a comprehensive waste management 
framework under the EMS Programme (ISO 14001) across all 
our facilities. This framework focuses on minimising waste 
generation and improving resource efficiency throughout 
our operations. Regular internal and external audits are 
carried out to identify areas of improvement, particularly in 
purchasing, enabling us to create targeted action plans to 
reduce waste.
Advancing circularity through alternative raw materials
In alignment with our aspirational goal of becoming 
carbon negative by 2040, we made significant strides 
in promoting circular economy principles, particularly 
through the enhanced use of alternative raw materials 
(ARMs) in cement production. By integrating industrial 
by-products such as fly ash, slag, red mud, and gypsum 
waste into our raw mix, we have reduced dependency 
on natural minerals and contributed meaningfully to 
emissions reduction leading to landfill avoidance for many 
countries. This strategic shift is deeply embedded in our operations and supply chain, fostering industrial symbiosis 
and driving process innovation. Our commitment 
to resource efficiency and waste utilisation reflects 
environmental responsibility and strategic value creation. 
Between FY2019 and FY2025, our alternative raw material 
consumption rate rose from 28% to 40%—a substantial 
achievement at both national and global levels—
underscoring our leadership in embedding circularity into 
core business practices.CASE STUDY
Natural Capital
Water stewardship
Water stewardship is at the core of our strategy, focused on 
enhancing water efficiency, conservation and responsible 
management across operations. Water efficiency programmes 
assess water usage, identify areas of improvement and 
implement water-saving initiatives while also enhancing 
wastewater treatment to ensure sustainable water use. Clear 
targets have been set to reduce water consumption, promote 
water recycling and raise employee awareness about effective 
water management practices through the Environmental 
Management System (EMS 14001).
Water management strategy
Our water stewardship initiatives integrate efficiency and 
conservation from the design phase. From using air-cooled 
condensers in power plants to reducing water consumption, 
promoting drip irrigation in local communities, optimising 
agricultural water use and implementing rainwater harvesting 
to enhance water availability, our water management strategy 
ensures sustainable use of water.
We also assess water quality and quantity risks for both 
existing and new facilities using third-party tools, conduct 
local facility-level evaluations to address potential regulatory 
changes. This year, we have reduced our specific water 
consumption from 171 to 167 litres per tonne of cementitious 
material (including CPP and colony), reinforcing our emphasis 
on a comprehensive water management strategy.

Sustainable mining practices
Our sustainable mining approach minimises environmental 
impact and enhances efficiency. By utilising advanced 
technologies, optimising resources, repurposing waste, 
and implementing energy-efficient practices, we ensure 
responsible operations that support local communities and 
long-term sustainability.
Technological advancements in mining
We integrate cutting-edge technologies to boost mining 
operation efficiency. IoT-based fleet monitoring provides 
real-time data to optimise machinery performance, reducing 
downtime. The Operator Independent Truck Dispatch System 
(OITDS) ensures optimal dump truck routing, maximising 
resource utilisation. Automation in drilling and blasting 
improves accuracy and operational efficiency.
Circular economy in mining
We incorporate circular economy principles by repurposing 
waste rock for civil construction, reducing waste and 
maximising material value from mining.
Energy efficiency and emission reduction
Energy efficiency is a focus in our operations. We have 
introduced Electric Vehicle (EV) dump trucks and plan to 
implement this across all units. By using fuel-efficient machinery 
and monitoring emissions, we significantly reduce our carbon 
footprint while adhering to environmental regulations.
Broadening the scope of value creation
• Extending water conservation and harvesting initiatives beyond operational boundaries
• Promoting the plantation of indigenous tree species
• Supporting organic farming and adopting water-efficient agricultural practices
• Delivering clean energy solutions to communities beyond our immediate vicinityWater management practices
We prioritise responsible water management to minimise 
ecosystem impact. Our operations do not depend on external 
water sources; instead, we utilise water reservoirs in mined-
out pits. Our Effluent Treatment Plants (ETP) recycle up to 
80% of water used, and rainwater harvesting systems support 
surrounding communities for agricultural and utility use.

covering financial, operational,

subordinate development and 
special projectsPerformance assessment

and quantitative feedback on

Result Areas (KRAs)

feedback and discussion 
with the appraisee and then 
assigns a score based on actual 
achievement against the set 
targets during goal settingFinal closure
• KRA score reflects actual 
achievement of goals set at the 
start of the performance period
• Ratings are normalised before 
appraisal letters are distributed

Worker welfare
Worker welfare is a priority for us, and we focus on promoting 
the overall well-being of our workforce. Key initiatives include 
providing proper facilities, addressing workplace concerns 
through open dialogues, ensuring fair compensation and 
benefits, and fostering an environment of trust, respect, 
and support. To ensure the safety of all employees, we 
continuously enhance our safety protocols and review 
procedures to prevent incidents. In FY25, we reported zero 
indirect fatalities. During this period, there were ten high-
consequence work-related injuries, direct fatalities, and work-
related ill-health fatalities, along with recordable work-related 
ill-health cases. The lost time injury frequency rate stood at 
0.13, reflecting our ongoing commitment to workplace safety.
Additionally, we recorded 9,019 near-miss incidents, 
each carefully reviewed to drive safety improvements. 
These evaluations led to significant outcomes such 
as enhanced safety standards, improved daily safety 
observations, strengthened machine guarding, reduced 
exposure to hazards, and reinforced structural integrity of 
plants. We also focused on regular structural inspections,  
job-specific training for critical tasks, and trade-specific 
training for key roles. We remain dedicated to building a 
zero accident workplace and consistently prioritise the health, 
safety, and well-being of our workforce.
  Engineers at our Lanka plant
Incident investigation and safety  
improvement process
At Dalmia Bharat, we follow a thorough 8-step incident 
investigation process to ensure continuous improvements 
in safety. This includes reporting the incident and providing 
an immediate response, forming the investigation 
team, collecting facts, conducting root cause analysis, 
identifying system weaknesses, making recommendations, 
documenting and communicating findings, and reviewing 
the recommendations.
The outcomes of these investigations are integrated into 
our safety management system through updating safety 
protocols (such as standards, HIRA, and SOPs), providing 
training and raising awareness, continuously monitoring 
the implementation of recommendations, and enhancing 
our safety culture. Through this approach, we ensure that 
every incident investigation leads to meaningful safety 
improvements, contributing to a safer work environment 
for all employees.

QR code system for emergency  
preparedness
We introduced a QR code system across our facility 
to enhance emergency preparedness and improve 
response times. The system, implemented at strategic 
locations, enables employees to quickly scan and 
access essential emergency information, including 
contact numbers, evacuation plans, and safety 
procedures. By replacing outdated printed materials 
with easily accessible digital content, we ensured that 
all emergency information is always up-to-date and 
readily available. This initiative not only helps reduce 
confusion during emergencies but also ensures that 
employees can act quickly and efficiently when needed. 
The QR code system has proven to be a crucial step 
in modernising our workplace safety measures and 
enhancing our emergency response capabilities.CASE STUDYRoad safety
Safe driving practices are essential to our operations, ensuring 
both employee well-being and logistics efficiency. To enhance 
road safety, we have established Logistics Safety Committees 
and implemented a comprehensive Road Safety Standard and 
Truck Yard Management Guideline. Leveraging technologies 
such as GPS tracking, RFID systems, and CCTV monitoring, 
we improve fleet visibility and control. GPS tracking allows 
us to monitor driver behaviour, identify unsafe practices like 
speeding or harsh braking, and gather data to tailor targeted 
safety training. It also helps reduce driver fatigue, minimise 
time on hazardous routes, and enable quick responses to 
accidents or breakdowns. RFID systems further improve 
safety by tracking vehicle and driver details, turnaround 
times, and access control.
In addition to these technologies, we prioritise driver 
training, regular vehicle inspections, medical camps, and 
incentive programmes to promote responsible driving. 
Our safety culture is reinforced through regular safety 
audits, incident reporting and analysis, and continuous 
safety training. Leadership commitment, employee 
engagement, and the use of technology, including e-learning, 
ensure that safety practices are consistently monitored and 
reinforced. Recognition and rewards programmes further 
support our efforts to maintain a safer and more efficient 
work environment.
Enhancing safety through digital learning
We implemented a digital learning platform to improve 
workplace safety by offering engaging and interactive 
training. The platform, accessible on all devices, 
allows employees to complete safety training at their 
convenience. We customised the content to address 
the specific safety needs of different departments and 
incorporated quizzes and real-life scenarios to enhance 
engagement. As a result, we have seen a marked 
improvement in safety awareness, with fewer accidents 
and greater compliance with safety standards across 
the organisation.CASE STUDY
Driver management
Road safety is a critical focus for us, and we take

Safety is central to our fleet management approach,

Defensive driving training for new drivers
Preventing accidents is a priority, and to achieve this, we 
conduct specialised defensive driving training for all newly 
onboarded drivers. These sessions, led by our DMCs, focus 
on increasing driver awareness, anticipating hazards, and 
making safe decisions. Our goal is to instil a comprehensive 
understanding of defensive driving.
Audio-visual safety training for drivers  
and contract workers
Our Company’s safety management system is designed to 
uphold the highest standards, ensuring that drivers and 
contractual staff understand and follow essential safety 
protocols. To enhance learning and retention, we conduct 
immersive training sessions that cover safety standards, 
expected behaviours and best practices. These sessions use 
videos, animations and multimedia resources, creating a 
multi-sensory learning experience. By adopting this approach, 
we effectively communicate critical safety information and 
utilise engaging audio-visual training.
Safety infrastructure
We invest in advanced safety infrastructure, including model 
areas, signage, traffic controls, vehicle inspection facilities, 
and road safety monitoring technologies. Alongside safety 
induction and training for all new employees and contractors, 
these efforts strengthen our overall safety infrastructure, 
reinforcing our commitment to road safety.
In-house static discharge safety solution
To address fire safety risks during the unloading of 
coal fines and fly ash, we developed a cost-effective 
static discharge kit. The kit includes a 24-volt relay and 
interlock system to ensure proper grounding before 
starting compressor operations. This solution, which 
was developed in-house, eliminated the risk of static 
discharge and significantly reduced costs compared 
to market alternatives. The new safety procedure has 
helped prevent fire hazards, improving overall safety 
during the unloading process.CASE STUDYHuman Capital
Safety recognition programme
The Monthly Safety Incentives and Recognition Programme 
motivates employees to improve safety performance by 
emphasising positive reinforcement, peer recognition, and 
tangible rewards. It encourages continuous improvement, 
strengthens our safety culture, and boosts morale, all of 
which contribute to a safer and more engaged workplace.
Health and safety in mining
The health and safety of our workers is a top priority. 
All personnel working in mining operations undergo 
Initial Medical Examinations (IME) and Periodical Medical 
Examinations (PME) in line with ILO guidelines to ensure 
their well-being. To mitigate respiratory risks, we conduct 
regular health screenings, including spirometry and X-rays 
every three years, and take follow-up measures based on the 
findings. Notably, no silicosis cases were reported in FY25. 
We also carry out regular pre-employment and periodical 
medical check-ups, respiratory health monitoring, hearing 
conservation programmes, and medical surveillance, 
maintaining comprehensive health records. Additionally, 
we have a robust system in place to monitor the issuance 
of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), ensuring consistent 
compliance and safety. Furthermore, we conduct annual safety training programmes to equip our workforce with 
the necessary skills and knowledge to manage operational 
risks effectively. Through these preventive measures and 
screenings, we effectively reduce occupational health risks 
and ensure the well-being of our workforce.

Sustainable livelihoods
We are committed to creating sustainable and resilient communities by supporting them to explore various avenues for 
livelihood opportunities. Our efforts include skill training in both the non-farm and farm sectors, promoting Self-Help Groups 
(SHGs), supporting farmer-producer organisations, and encouraging traditional crafts. By establishing small social enterprises, 
we empower youth, women and farmers, guiding them towards increased income and long-term economic stability.
Empowering rural communities through 
sustainable livelihoods
India’s workforce is undergoing a significant 
transformation, yet a substantial skill gap remains, as 
highlighted by the National Skill Development Corporation’s 
(NSDC) skill need report. Recognising this, Dalmia Bharat 
Foundation (DBF) launched the DIKSHa (Dalmia Institute 
of Knowledge and Skill Harnessing) programme in 2016 
to equip rural youth with industry-relevant skills, creating 
pathways for sustainable livelihoods. Starting with a single 
center, DIKSHa has grown to 19 centres across India, 
located near Dalmia Bharat Group’s plant operations, 
providing critical training in various trades.
19 
DIKSHa centres across India
A key focus of DIKSHa is empowering women through 
skills training. Initially, DBF faced challenges in attracting 
female trainees, as conventional trades often did not 
align with their comfort and aspirations. To address this, 
DIKSHa introduced women-friendly courses like assistant 
beauty therapist, sewing machine operator, and home 
health aide, providing a safe and supportive learning 
environment. This approach has significantly increased 
female participation, with over 50% of all trainees now 
being women.
50%
Women traineesHowever, a critical hurdle remained – many women 
were hesitant to migrate for employment due to safety 
concerns. Understanding this, DBF implemented an 
innovative solution where a dedicated staff member 
accompanies female trainees to their joining locations, 
helping them complete formalities and easing their 
transition into the workforce. This support system has 
greatly improved retention rates, ensuring long-term 
employment stability. Unlike conventional programmes 
that offer only three months of post-placement support, 
DIKSHa provides a full year of guidance, reinforcing 
the Foundation’s commitment to building secure and 
sustainable careers for women across India.
As DIKSHa continues to expand, it embodies the spirit of 
being Strong, Secure and Sustainable . By empowering 
women to overcome barriers, build confidence, and secure 
meaningful livelihoods, DIKSHa is not just transforming 
individual lives but also fostering resilient communities, 
paving the way for a brighter and more inclusive future.CASE STUDY  DIKSHa trainees of Schnerider Electrical, post their training completion, Rajgangpur (Odisha)

The Dalmia Institute of Knowledge and Skill Harnessing 
(DIKSHa) programme, launched in 2016 with a commitment 
to ‘Giving Back to Society’, aims to provide industry-aligned 
skill training to youth in communities near our business 
operations. DBF identified relevant sectors of training such 
as healthcare, retail, IT and more based on the pan India, skill 
gap analysis done by National Skill Development Corporation 
(NSDC) and initiated placement linked skill training through 
DIKSHa. With 19 centres across 9 states, DIKSHa has the 
capacity to train 5,700 youth annually. Additionally, we 
support two ITIs in Dalmiapuram and Rajgangpur and manage 
two government ITIs under the public-private partnership 
model. In FY25, DIKSHa successfully trained a significant 
number of youths, with a focus on gender equality. Our one 
year post placement support ensures that candidates receive 
mentorship and guidance for career success. DIKSHa plans to 
open three more centres in FY26 to empower rural youth with 
valuable skills and improve employment opportunities.

Water conservation initiatives
Through Dalmia Bharat Foundation, we are committed 
to addressing climate change by focusing on sustainable 
water management and resource conservation. Our efforts 
include building water harvesting structures, restoring water 
bodies and raising awareness about water conservation. 
These initiatives aim to improve water availability for

recharge and long-term water security.

Water impact assessment
The Impact Assessment of our water conservation projects 
was carried out by CII - Centre of Excellence for Sustainable 
Development (CESD). These initiatives focused on improving 
water management and availability in rural areas. The key 
interventions included:• Creation of check dams
• Desilting of ponds
• Recharge shafts
• Strengthening of village pond bunds
Outcomes
• A significant 73% of respondents expressed a positive 
view of DBF, with 44% rating it as ’Good’ and 29% 
considering it ‘Excellent’.
• Compared to 58% in the control group, only 30% of 
respondents in the treatment group reported facing 
issues with water availability.
• Furthermore, 54% of the treatment group agreed that 
groundwater levels have increased, compared to 38% in 
the control group.
• With the introduction of water structures, 10% more 
respondents are now growing three crops instead 
of just one. Additionally, 5% of respondents began 
growing two crops, whereas the number of people 
growing only one crop decreased from 46% to 31%.• The use of village ponds and farm ponds for irrigation 
has risen by 13% post-construction, with borewells 
increasing by 5%, wells by 2% and canals by 1%.
• Following the construction of water harvesting 
structures, 61% of respondents reported that their 
quality of life has improved, reflecting the effectiveness 
of the water conservation initiatives.
• 75% of respondents indicated that the water-related 
infrastructure is in good working condition, with only 
9% mentioning the need for repairs or reconstruction.
Testimonials

Nation building through conservation  
of national heritage
Dalmia Bharat’s role as 'Monument Mitra'
As part of the Government of India’s ‘Adopt a Heritage’  
initiative, Dalmia Bharat Limited was selected as a 
‘Monument Mitra’ to upgrade tourist infrastructure at the 
iconic Red Fort in Delhi. In collaboration with the Ministry of 
Tourism, Ministry of Culture and the Archaeological Survey 
of India (ASI), Dalmia Bharat has enhanced the monument’s 
visitor experience through state-of-the-art amenities and 
immersive storytelling, positioning the Red Fort as a world-
class cultural destination. The initiative was undertaken in 
collaboration with our implementation partner, Sabhyata 
Foundation, under the 'Adopt a Heritage' programme.Social and Relationship Capital
Red Fort Visitor Centre  
(launched in August 2022)
Located in a restored 19th-century British barrack, the Centre 
offers an introduction to the fort through:
• A museum covering nine key zones of the Red Fort
• A 360° immersive show
• Augmented reality photography zone
• Cafeteria and souvenir shop
‘Jai Hind’ Sound & Light Show  
(launched in January 2023)
Developed in partnership with the Sabhyata Foundation, 
the Jai Hind show is a live, multi-sensory performance that 
narrates India’s journey from the Mughal era to modern 
times. Blending projection mapping, light and sound effects, 
dance, live-action sequences, and life-size puppetry, the show 
is narrated as ‘Waqt’, in the voice of Amitabh Bachchan.
Social and Relationship Capital
Performances are held at Naubat Khana, Diwan-e-Aam 
and Diwan-e-Khas. The show brings alive key historical 
events, including:
• Dara Shikoh and Aurangzeb’s power struggle
• Nadir Shah’s invasion
• The rise of the Marathas
• The 1857 War of Independence
• INA trials and India’s freedom movement
Guests move through each site, with the final 35-40 minutes 
presented as a seated experience in the Diwan-e-Khas lawns.
Adopt a Heritage 2.0
The Ministry of Tourism has launched 'Adopt a Heritage 2.0', 
aimed at developing and enhancing tourist infrastructure 
across a wider range of monuments in India. Under this 
initiative, Sabhyata Foundation, an organisation committed 
to preserving and promoting India’s cultural and heritage 
ecosystem, and delivering world-class heritage experiences, 
has been designated as a 'Smarak Saarthi' for four iconic 
landmarks in Delhi: Purana Qila, Mehrauli Archaeological Park, 
Safdarjung Tomb, and Humayun’s Tomb. In this unique role, 
the Foundation is contributing significantly to Delhi’s cultural 
landscape by promoting responsible tourism, upgrading heritage sites with improved facilities and amenities, and 
fostering a deeper public appreciation for India’s rich history. 
Dalmia Bharat Limited is working in partnership with Sabhyata 
Foundation in this initiative.
Currently, enhancement work is underway to improve basic 
visitor amenities at Purana Qila, Humayun’s Tomb, and 
Safdarjung Tomb. Additionally, there are ongoing explorations 
into event production and allied services at Purana Qila.
Key objectives of this Project are:

Recycling and waste management
To ensure proper recycling, all plastic scrap is sold exclusively to CPCB EPR-certified recyclers. Any packaging material that is 
damaged during production is stored and later auctioned off to certified recyclers. In addition, we have long-term partnerships 
with industries and municipalities to collect and incinerate waste in our kilns, to effectively manage the entire lifecycle of 
plastic waste.We follow Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)

Management Discussion 
and Analysis
Prelude
Dalmia Bharat Limited is one of India’s leading cement 
manufacturers, serving markets across 23 states. 
Our extensive manufacturing footprint, comprising 
15 integrated plants and grinding units across 10 states, 
is strategically located to ensure optimal service to key 
markets. This is supported by a resilient and efficient supply 
chain that enables smooth movement of raw materials and 
finished products, strengthening our ability to respond to 
market demand while maintaining high service levels.
With this robust infrastructure in place, we have steadily 
scaled our production capacity to meet the growing needs 
of India’s infrastructure and housing sectors. As of FY25, our 
total installed capacity stands at 49.5 MTPA, achieved through 
a combination of strategic acquisitions and both greenfield 
and brownfield expansions. We are now focused on reaching 
75 MnT, our next milestone in the medium term in line with 
our vision to become pan-India company in due course.
Our product portfolio is anchored by trusted brands such 
as Dalmia Cement, Dalmia DSP, Dalmia Supreme and Konark 
Cement, each tailored to address specific customer segments Global economic overview
The global economy grew by 3.3% in 2024, supported by 
regional recoveries and the easing of inflation, driven by 
improved supply chains and falling food and energy prices. 
Although the world economy remains on a positive trajectory, 
it is influenced by evolving trade dynamics and policy 
shifts in key economies.
In 2024, the volume of world merchandise trade expanded 
by 2.9%, and commercial services trade grew by 6.8%. 
Merchandise exports rose by 2% to US$ 24.43 trillion, while 
service exports increased by 9% to US$ 8.69 trillion, driven 
by strong global demand and the easing of supply chain 
disruptions. This rise in global trade was also supported by 
increased demand for services and industrial raw materials 
as industries ramped up production, particularly across 
Asia and Africa.
(Source: WTO Blog, April 2025 )
However, the dynamics of global trade have shifted due to 
the United States’ implementation of new trade policies, 
notably the imposition of additional tariffs, and the 
subsequent responses from its trading partners. Economists 
and policymakers are closely monitoring the impacts across 
sectors and industries. The full effect on the global economy 
remains to be seen as nations adjust and adapt.
The global inflation rate stood at approximately 5.3% in 2024 
and is expected to moderate to 4.3% in 2025 and 3.6% in 
2026. This moderation is attributed to factors such as easing 
supply chain pressures, reduced energy price volatility, and 
the effects of monetary tightening. However, inflation in 
emerging markets is projected to remain higher than the 
global average due to domestic economic factors, including 
currency depreciation and evolving global trade dynamics.
(Source: Reuters/IMF, April 2025 )
Prices of fuel commodities are projected to decline by 7.9% 
in 2025, with oil and coal prices moderating by 15.5% and 
15.8%, respectively. However, natural gas prices are expected 
to surge by 22.8%, driven by continued disruptions in supply 
chains from Russia through Ukraine. Crude oil prices are 
forecasted to average US$ 66.94 per barrel in 2025 and 
US$ 62.38 per barrel in 2026.
(Source: IMF World Economic Outlook, April 2025 )

Outlook

Projected GDP growth in 2025
Global growth is expected to moderate to 2.8% in 2025, 
driven by ongoing trade tensions, tight monetary policies, 
and persistent geopolitical risks. The moderation also reflects 
structural changes in global supply chains. A gradual recovery 
is anticipated in 2026, with growth projected to improve 
to 3.0%. Global inflation is expected to ease in 2025, with 
advanced economies likely to experience a faster decline in 
inflation rates compared to emerging markets. Commodity 
prices, particularly for energy, are projected to decline, 
while non-fuel commodity prices are expected to rise.

economies but remain tighter in emerging markets due to 
trade uncertainties and currency pressures. Central banks 
in advanced economies are expected to continue gradual 
monetary policy easing over the coming quarters.
Source: IMF WEO, April 2024
Indian economic overview
India’s economy is estimated to grow at 6.5% in FY2024-25, 
moderating from the robust 9.2% growth recorded in the 
previous fiscal year. India remained the fastest-growing major 
economy amid global uncertainty, demonstrating strong 
resilience. Growth moderated partly due to a high base effect 
from the previous year, subdued private investment, tighter 
financial conditions, and ongoing global trade uncertainties. 
The general elections in FY25 led to a temporary pause in 
infrastructure spending and policy rollout, contributing 
to softer cement demand. Despite these factors, robust   Kadapa Cement Unit, Andhra Pradesh
